community.headline: Maldon Mud Race sponsor gives Basildon Hospital two Xbox gaming trolleys for young patients
community.summary: A £3,060 gift from JR Revell Ltd pays for portable consoles that can be wheeled to children's and teenagers' bedsides.
body: Basildon Hospital now has two portable Xbox gaming trolleys for children and teenagers, paid for by a £3,060 donation from JR Revell Ltd, main sponsor of the Maldon Mud Race. The trolleys can be wheeled to bedsides, so they also reach young patients too unwell to leave their rooms or who must isolate.

The firm chose Basildon because the partner of its operations manager, Ronnie Baker, works on two of the hospital's children's wards. This year's Mud Race raised more than £50,000 for local charities, and JR Revell entered its own team to add to the total.

One trolley will go in a new teen room being refurbished on the ward, and the other will move between the children's wards. Southend and Broomfield hospitals already have similar trolleys, which the trust says have proved popular.

community.headline: Volunteers wanted for Tesco winter food collection on 26 to 28 November

body: Foodbanks and food charities are looking for volunteers to stand at collection points in large Tesco stores for the supermarket's Winter Food Collection, which runs from 26 to 28 November. Volunteering takes about three hours, and the charities say having people in store significantly increases how much food is given.

This is the 14th year of the collection, run with charity partners Trussell and Felix, and last year shoppers donated almost 1.5 million meals' worth of food. One in five Trussell food parcels comes from Tesco and its customers, and more than half of the charities in the Felix network, which spans over 8,000 local groups, report rising demand over the past year.

People can sign up through the Trussell or Felix websites to help at their nearest large Tesco. Trussell's co-chief executive Matthew van Duyvenbode said volunteers were urgently needed to play their part.

official.headline: Planning inspectors begin public hearings on Chelmsford's Local Plan at the Civic Centre
official.summary: Inspectors are testing the blueprint for homes, jobs, schools and roads over the next 15 years, with sessions open to the public.
body: Independent Planning Inspectors began examining Chelmsford's new Local Plan at the Civic Centre on Tuesday 10 November, Chelmsford City Council says. The plan sets out where new homes, jobs, schools, roads and green spaces could go across the city over the next 15 years, while protecting landscapes, heritage and community facilities.

The council submitted the plan to the Secretary of State in June 2026. People who asked for changes during the earlier consultations may be invited to speak or send written statements, and the council says both carry equal weight. Cllr Richard Lee, Cabinet Member for Planning and Place-Shaping, said the council was confident the plan was a clear blueprint for the homes, jobs and infrastructure the city needs.

Members of the public can watch from the public gallery or follow a live stream. After the hearings the Inspectors will publish a report on whether the plan is legally sound, with any changes needed, which will then go to Full Council and a public consultation.

body: Southend-on-Sea City Council has opened the final round of public consultation on its draft Local Plan, the document that will guide where new homes, employment land, infrastructure and community facilities may go across the city. It runs from Friday 6 November until Monday 21 December 2026.

The council said central government formally directed it on 23 October to publish the draft for consultation by 6 November, and the cabinet agreed unanimously on 5 November to do so. Comments at this stage must address whether the plan is legally compliant and sound under national planning policy. Cllr Kevin Robinson, cabinet member for planning, property and governance, urged residents to read the draft and respond.

Documents and the response form are on the council's Local Plan website, with paper copies at Southend libraries and the Civic Centre reception. Full council is due to consider the final plan in early 2027, when it will be submitted for independent examination by a planning inspector.

body: Colchester City Council's grounds maintenance service transferred to Amphora, the company the council wholly owns, on 1 November. The service looks after parks, sports grounds, open spaces, housing land, cemeteries and the crematorium across the city.

Around 40 former Idverde employees moved across, and council and Amphora staff marked the change with volunteering days at Castle Park on 2 and 3 November, clearing leaves and planting hundreds of spring bulbs. The service covers almost 13,000 assets over more than 870 hectares. Cllr Martin Goss, portfolio holder for waste, neighbourhoods and leisure, welcomed the new colleagues into the council family.
The council says the arrangement gives it more flexibility to respond to local priorities and to find new ways of improving parks and green spaces, while keeping investment in the local area.

body: Essex Police is appealing for witnesses after men claiming to be police officers approached people in Tilbury between 4am and 4.45am on Saturday 7 November. Police say the men were not in uniform and showed no identification, and nobody was hurt.

In one incident near the Tesco Express on Calcutta Road, two men got out of a white car and took a man's wallet and keys, police said. Officers say a taxi driver was also targeted on St Chads Road and another man was approached in the area. Police described three men, one in a high-visibility jacket and two in dark tracksuits, using a large white SUV-style car.

Grays CID is asking anyone who saw anything, or who was driving in the area with a dash cam, to come forward. Police say genuine officers will show their warrant card when asked and understand if people want to check their identity.

stories.summary: A mixed Saturday for the Essex clubs in the Isthmian Premier Division, with one away win, two draws and a heavy defeat on the Kent coast.
body: Maldon & Tiptree produced the best Essex result of the day in the Isthmian Premier Division, winning 3-1 away at Wingate & Finchley on Saturday. Brentwood Town came away from Three Bridges with a 1-1 draw, while Stanway Rovers and Whitehawk finished goalless.

Aveley had a much harder afternoon, losing 4-0 at promotion-chasing Ramsgate in front of a crowd of 1,444. Billy Munday headed the hosts in front inside two minutes from an Alfie Paxman corner, and Rowan Liburd made it two on 15 minutes after Aveley goalkeeper Jamie Grossart dropped the ball at his feet. Paxman added a third on 77 minutes and Latrell Lewis struck in the 90th, while Ramsgate keeper Jonny Henly also saved a penalty from Malachi Napa.

The defeat leaves Aveley fifteenth in the table. Their next game is away at Hutton in the Essex Senior Cup on Wednesday 11 November, and they return to league action at Carshalton on Saturday 21 November.

stories.headline: Braintree Town beaten 4-1 by Weston-super-Mare in National League South
stories.summary: Luke Coulson struck twice before half-time for the hosts at the Optima Stadium, and Hubbard's late goal was only a consolation for the Iron.
body: Braintree Town suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat away to Weston-super-Mare in the National League South on Saturday. The Iron were three goals down within eight minutes of the restart and could not find a way back.

Weston had a goal from Ollie Hulbert ruled out for offside before Luke Coulson opened the scoring from around 30 yards with a deflected effort on 33 minutes. Coulson then converted a penalty on the stroke of half-time after Will Jenkins Davies was tripped, Hulbert made it three on 53 minutes and Jenkins Davies added a fourth six minutes later.
Hubbard pulled a goal back for Braintree on 86 minutes, and Louis Britton dragged a late one-on-one chance over the bar for the home side. The game was watched by a crowd of 962.

stories.summary: Danny Cowley's U's beat the non-league visitors at the JobServe Community Stadium on Saturday to stay in the competition.
body: Colchester United are through to the FA Cup second round after a 1-0 win over Worcester City at the JobServe Community Stadium on Saturday 7 November. The Daily Gazette and the club both reported the win, which keeps the U's in the competition.

Before the first-round tie, midfielder Paul Digby, 31 and back in the Colchester side, told the Gazette the players knew how big the game was for Worcester. He has plenty of experience of the competition, including a third-round upset, and said he loves the FA Cup.

stories.headline: Chelmsford Chieftains lose 6-5 to Swindon Wildcats 2 after a shootout
stories.summary: Sasha Maltsev was named man of the match after scoring twice, including a shorthanded goal, at the Link Centre in West Swindon.
body: Chelmsford Chieftains were beaten 6-5 by Swindon Wildcats 2 on Saturday night, with the NIHL National game settled by a penalty shootout. The two sides could not be separated through regulation and overtime, finishing level at 5-5.
Grant Bartlett, Lane Paddison twice and Sasha Maltsev twice scored for the Chieftains. Maltsev's second goal came while Chelmsford were shorthanded, and he was named the visitors' man of the match.
The sides were level at 1-1 after the first period, and Swindon held a 4-3 lead going into the third before Chelmsford drew level at 5-5.

stories.headline: Isthmian North: Buckhurst Hill win 3-0 at Bowers & Pitsea as Witham Town triumph at Redbridge
stories.summary: Two away wins for Essex clubs headlined Saturday in the Isthmian North, while Takeley and Little Oakley were both beaten 1-0 at home.
body: Buckhurst Hill produced the standout Essex result in the Isthmian North on Saturday, winning 3-0 away at Bowers & Pitsea. Witham Town also won on the road, beating Redbridge 2-1.

stories.headline: Elliot Long double earns Billericay Town a 2-2 draw at Dagenham & Redbridge
stories.summary: Danny Scopes' side twice found the net through their striker and held on for a point against the Daggers in the National League South.
body: Billericay Town came away from Dagenham & Redbridge with a 2-2 draw in the National League South on Saturday. Elliot Long scored both goals for Billericay, who had to dig in after the break to protect a share of the points.

Long put Billericay ahead on 27 minutes before Henry Hawkins levelled for the hosts three minutes before half-time. Beautyman then gave Dagenham the lead from the penalty spot on 55 minutes, but Long struck again on 68 minutes to make it 2-2.
Billericay manager Danny Scopes was pleased with what he saw from his players. "I'm delighted with the team performance," he said after the game.

stories.summary: Goals from Clarke and a Barham penalty turned the game around at the Dunmow Group Community Stadium after Max Ehmer had put the visitors ahead.
body: Chelmsford City fought back from a goal down to beat Farnborough 2-1 in the National League South on Saturday. The Clarets trailed at half-time but scored twice after the break to take all three points in front of their home supporters.

Farnborough captain Max Ehmer opened the scoring on 34 minutes. Clarke levelled six minutes into the second half, finishing after a run and cross from Barham, and Barham then struck from the penalty spot on 70 minutes to put City in front.

It was an eventful afternoon for Odegah, who had an early header ruled out for offside and was later booked for simulation after going down in the box. City saw out the closing minutes to secure the win, watched by a crowd of 1,523.

stories.headline: Southend mark 20 years since Eastwood sank Manchester United, as Sam Austin rejoins Kidderminster on loan
stories.summary: BBC Essex revisits the night Roots Hall beat Sir Alex Ferguson's side in the League Cup, while forward Sam Austin heads back to Aggborough for the rest of the season.
body: Saturday marks 20 years since Southend United beat Manchester United 1-0 at Roots Hall in the fourth round of the League Cup, on 7 November 2006. Freddy Eastwood's 27th-minute free-kick settled the tie in front of 11,532 fans, with Southend then bottom of the Championship, and BBC Essex has released a four-part podcast in which those involved relive the win.

Sir Alex Ferguson made nine changes but still fielded ten internationals, including Wayne Rooney and Cristiano Ronaldo, who was twice denied by goalkeeper Darryl Flahavan. Then manager Steve Tilson recalled that the players feared the worst when they saw the teamsheet. Southend went on to take Tottenham to extra time in the quarter-final before losing to a Jermain Defoe goal.

In current squad news, the club confirmed on Thursday that Sam Austin has joined Kidderminster Harriers on loan, and Kidderminster say the move runs until the end of the season. Austin, who left Aggborough four years ago for Notts County, told the Harriers he had always kept a place in his heart for the club and felt the timing was right.

stories.headline: More than 23 years of jail terms over Epping Bell Hotel disorder after Loughton man, 34, is locked up
stories.summary: Keith Silk was given two years and 11 months at Chelmsford Crown Court for violent disorder and criminal damage outside the hotel.
body: Keith Silk, of Torrington Drive, Loughton, was convicted after a trial on 1 June of violent disorder and criminal damage over the protest outside the Bell Hotel in Epping on 17 July 2025, Your Harlow and the BBC report. He was jailed at Chelmsford Crown Court on Tuesday.

The BBC reports that Silk threw a beer bottle at a police van and tried to pull a hotel sign out of the ground, and prosecutor Harriet Palfreman said he threatened officers. His barrister said he had been experiencing sensory overload, but Judge Alexander Mills said Silk chose to stay and placed himself at the heart of events.

Essex Police figures reported by Your Harlow put immediate custody over the protest at more than 23 years, while 11 others have received community orders, fines or suspended sentences. Chief Inspector Terry Fisher said the disorder left the community scared and anxious.

stories.headline: Man in his 80s dies after car hits two pedestrians in Mount Bures, near Colchester
stories.summary: A woman in her 70s is still being treated in hospital after Sunday's collision on Hall Road, and police are appealing for footage.
body: A man in his 80s has died after he and a woman were struck by a car on Hall Road in Mount Bures at about 1pm on Sunday, the BBC reports. He died the following day, and the woman, in her 70s, is still receiving hospital treatment.
Essex Police said no arrests had been made and asked anyone with information, CCTV or dash cam footage to come forward.

stories.headline: Armistice Day in Thurrock: two-minute silence at Stifford's Ardale memorial and evening maritime service at Tilbury
stories.summary: Thurrock Council has listed two Armistice Day gatherings on Wednesday, one mid-morning in North Stifford and one in the evening at the Port of Tilbury.
body: Thurrock marks Armistice Day on Wednesday 11 November with two public acts of remembrance listed by Thurrock Council, three days after the borough's Remembrance Sunday services. The council's events page invites residents to both.

The first is at the Ardale War Memorial on Stifford Green, Guardian Avenue, North Stifford, from 10.50am, in time for the national two-minute silence at 11am. In the evening Forth Ports holds its annual Tilbury remembrance service, a maritime memorial, at the London International Cruise Terminal, with refreshments from 5pm and the service at 6pm.
On Sunday the council's list ran to more than a dozen services across the borough, from Grays High Street and Tilbury's Civic Square to East Tilbury's Bata War Memorial and South Ockendon.
points: Forth Ports' Tilbury service is at the London International Cruise Terminal

stories.summary: Castle Point Borough Council has hired Videre to install new cameras paid for by the police, fire and crime commissioner's Safer Streets Fund, with work due to finish in February 2027.
body: Castle Point Borough Council has appointed Videre to upgrade the borough's CCTV in a £1 million project funded by the Essex Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner's Safer Streets Fund, Greatest Hits Radio reports. Camera sites were chosen using police crime and antisocial behaviour data and local feedback, and the cameras will be monitored 24 hours a day from Southend City Council's control room. Work began in early November and is due to finish in February 2027.

Due to be finished in February 2027

body: Persimmon Homes Essex has asked Thurrock Council for outline permission to build up to 200 homes at Grey Goose Farm, north of Long Lane in Grays, half of them shared ownership or below-market rent. Sixteen of the 17 public comments lodged so far object, citing traffic, stretched GP and dental services and lost countryside.

stories.headline: Hidden faces, street drinking and e-scooters on footpaths could all bring fines in Harlow under council plans open until 5 January
stories.summary: Harlow Council wants residents' views on a package of Public Space Protection Orders, some town-wide and some for set places, with breaches punishable by fixed penalties or prosecution.
body: Harlow Council has opened a consultation on a wide package of Public Space Protection Orders aimed at antisocial behaviour, intimidation and nuisance, Your Harlow reports. Options include banning face coverings used to hide identity during antisocial behaviour, e-scooters and cycling in pedestrian areas, street drinking, public drug use and aggressive begging.

Some measures could apply across the town and others only in set places. Breaches could bring fixed penalty notices or prosecution, and council leader Dan Swords said Harlow would not be a soft touch. The consultation closes on 5 January before final proposals go to Cabinet.
points: Council officers trained as enforcers, backed by new CCTV

stories.headline: County Hall finance chief warns of 'existential threat' as Essex budget gap could reach £476m by 2030
stories.summary: Essex County Council's cabinet member for finance, Bo Davis, says the gap between spending and income will keep widening without action, with social care driving most of the pressure, as a public budget consultation runs until 6 December.
body: Essex County Council faces a budget gap of nearly £170 million in 2027/28 if no further action is taken, rising to £280 million the year after, £384 million in 2029/30 and £476 million by 2030/31, according to figures reported by the Local Democracy Reporting Service. Cabinet member for finance Bo Davis, of Reform UK, described it as the biggest threat the council had faced in a long time, and the council is asking residents where money should go in a consultation on its 2027/28 budget.

About 70 per cent of next year's pressure is in social care, with extra spending expected of £45 million on adult social care, £64 million on children's care, £32 million on children's placements and £15 million on home-to-school transport. The council's 2026/27 net cost of services came to about £1,437 million, roughly £56 million more than budgeted. Council leader Peter Harris has argued that the government's funding settlement has not been fair to Essex taxpayers.

Mr Davis said it was too early to discuss council tax, currently £1,641.96 for a Band D home, and that no decisions had been made; reserves of around £600 million would be used only for transformation or bridging where absolutely necessary. He has contacted the Liberal Democrat, Conservative and independent group leaders seeking cross-party work on savings. The consultation closes on 6 December and the cabinet is due to consider budget proposals on 15 January 2027.

Social care accounts for about 70% of next year's pressure
Band D council tax is £1,641.96; no decision on any change

stories.headline: Southend's fenced-off Three Shells Lagoon should be removed and the beach restored, council report says
stories.summary: Southend-on-Sea City Council says taking out the failed lagoon is its preferred long-term option, and the proposal goes to Cabinet on 16 November.
body: A council report recommends that the Three Shells Lagoon on Southend's seafront be removed and the site returned to a natural beach. Southend-on-Sea City Council says this is its preferred long-term option after a technical assessment of several possibilities, and that the Joint Administration has committed to resolving the long-running problems with the scheme.

The council said the lagoon has already used a significant amount of public money and remains fenced off and unusable despite past investment. Cllr Matt Dent, Cabinet Member for Business, Culture, Music and Tourism, described it as no longer fit for purpose and said the council needed to "cut our losses". The council's announcement did not give a cost for removal, but said no realistic option would avoid further substantial cost.
The proposal will be considered by the council's Cabinet on Monday 16 November 2026. The council published the report on 9 November, setting out the recommended way forward for the site.
points: Report recommends removing the lagoon structure and restoring a natural beach

stories.headline: Braintree and County Hall leaders vow to resist Home Office bid to keep Wethersfield asylum site open after April 2027
stories.summary: The government has applied to extend its use of the former airbase near Braintree, where asylum seekers have been housed since July 2023, and both councils say they will look at ways to oppose it.
body: The Home Office has applied to keep housing asylum seekers at MDP Wethersfield, the former airbase near Braintree, after its current permission runs out in April 2027, BBC News reports. The site has been in use since July 2023.

Braintree District Council leader Tom Cunningham said the site was still unsuitable and should close as soon as possible, while county council leader Peter Harris said the authority would review the application and consider every option to challenge further expansion.

stories.headline: Police seek doorbell and dash cam footage after young driver dies in Harlow crash at Kingsland
stories.summary: The man in his 20s was alone in a Ford Fiesta that hit a parked car shortly after 5.30am on Sunday, police said, and the road has since reopened.
body: A man in his 20s has died after a crash at Kingsland, at its junction with Tendring Road in Harlow, early on Sunday 8 November. Essex Police said his car hit a parked car and that several other vehicles nearby were damaged.

Emergency services were called shortly after 5.30am. The driver, who was alone in a Ford Fiesta, was pronounced dead at the scene, police said. The road was closed for several hours while officers carried out enquiries, and drivers had been asked to stay away.

Essex Police are appealing for anyone who saw the collision, or who has dash cam or doorbell camera footage from the area, to come forward to help establish how it happened. No other injuries have been reported.

Several parked vehicles were damaged and the road was shut for hours

stories.headline: Russell Brand, who grew up in Grays, could challenge his 10-and-a-half-year rape sentence, solicitor tells the Standard
stories.summary: A criminal defence solicitor not involved in the case told the Evening Standard an appeal against the sentence was the most likely next step, after the comedian was jailed at Southwark Crown Court on Monday.
body: Russell Brand, the comedian and actor who grew up in Grays and went to school in the town, has been jailed for 10 years and six months for one rape and three sexual assaults. Mr Justice Bennathan passed sentence at Southwark Crown Court on Monday 9 November, four days after a jury found him guilty following a four-week trial.

The judge gave nine years for the rape and a further year and a half for the sexual assaults, the Evening Standard reports. Brand will serve two-thirds of the term before he can be released on licence, and he will be on the sex offenders' register for life. The offences were committed against four women between 2004 and 2009; the jury cleared him of two counts of rape and one of attempted indecent assault.

Brand, 51, had spent four nights at HMP Wandsworth since the verdicts and was expected to return there. Raj Chada, head of criminal defence at the London firm Hodge Jones & Allen, who is not involved in the case, told the Standard an appeal against the sentence was the most likely route. The Metropolitan Police praised the women's courage, resilience and determination; all four are entitled to lifelong anonymity, and the Met has said it is still investigating two further allegations, with files sent to the Crown Prosecution Service.

stories.summary: Operation Machinize, coordinated by the National Crime Agency and carried out locally by Essex Police with partner agencies, targeted organised crime linked to businesses across the county.
body: Essex Police, Trading Standards, HMRC, Border Force, the Home Office and the Fair Work Agency visited more than 100 premises across the county under Operation Machinize, a National Crime Agency-led crackdown on organised crime, Greatest Hits Radio reports.

Officers seized £10,360 in cash, nearly 10,000 illicit cigarettes valued at about £5,540, 1kg of tobacco worth £575 and nine illegal vapes. Detective Chief Inspector Terry Balding said such businesses can look legitimate while facilitating serious criminality.

Nearly 10,000 illicit cigarettes taken off sale

stories.headline: Southend council still heading for a £12m overspend as one child's care placement tops £1m a year
stories.summary: The latest six-month forecast shows the gap narrowing by about £1.3m, but children's social care costs have climbed by around £1.5m since the summer.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council is forecasting an overspend of £11.96m for 2026/27, according to its latest figures covering the first six months of the financial year. That is about £1.3m better than earlier forecasts, but the council says rising children's placement costs are adding fresh strain.

Children's Services costs have risen by around £1.5m since the summer. One residential placement costs more than £1m a year and seven more cost over £500,000 each, and the council says children's and adult social care now account for more than all of the remaining pressure. Improvements in adult social care contributed about £1.3m to the better forecast, and most planned savings for the year have already been delivered.

Council leader Daniel Cowan said the council was under no illusion about the scale of the challenge in Children's Services. The council says it will tighten financial controls, speed up its Transformation Programme and keep pressing the Government for changes to social care funding.
points: Overspend forecast at £11.96m, down about £1.3m
Seven placements cost more than £500,000 a year each
Most planned savings for 2026/27 already delivered

stories.headline: Police still seeking witnesses to Sunday's early-hours crash that killed two people on Chelmsford's Copperfield Road
stories.summary: Essex Police wants doorbell, dashcam and eyewitness accounts after a driver and passenger died when their Ford Fiesta struck a property wall near Havisham Way.
body: Two people, the driver and a passenger, died when the car they were in struck a wall in Chelmsford in the early hours of Sunday 8 November. No other vehicle was involved.

Essex Police said it was called shortly after 1.45am to Copperfield Road, close to where it meets Havisham Way. The Ford Fiesta hit and damaged the wall of a property, and the road was closed for a time afterwards. The names of the two people who died have not been released.

Essex Police is asking anyone who saw the crash, or who has doorbell or dashcam footage from the area, to get in touch through its website or its 24/7 online Live Chat service. Greatest Hits Radio Essex and BBC News have both reported the appeal.

stories.headline: Harlow college shut over building safety fears wins approval for a permanent new school

body: Harlow Council's planning committee has unanimously approved designs for a new Sir Frederick Gibberd College on its existing Tendring Road site, with room for 1,200 secondary pupils and a 500-place sixth form, the BBC reports.

stories.headline: Retired Wethersfield camp teacher says Reform councillor Carl Johnson likened her to a Nazi collaborator, days after his deleted immigration post

body: Mair Godley, a 78-year-old retired teacher who taught English at the Wethersfield asylum camp, says Reform UK councillor Carl Johnson compared her to a Second World War Nazi collaborator at a recent district council meeting, ITV News Anglia reported. stories.headline: Maldon council says national rules leave little room to refuse new homes in Tollesbury, Great Totham and Latchingdon
stories.summary: The district's leader says unpopular village schemes cannot be turned down without sound planning evidence, as a new national scheme also takes many decisions away from committee.
body: Maldon District Council has responded to anger over housing decisions in Tollesbury, Great Totham and Latchingdon, saying national policy limits its ability to refuse development on the edge of villages. It says the Government's December 2024 change to the housing formula raised the district's annual need from 310 to 586 homes.

The council says the revised National Planning Policy Framework, published in August 2026, is more supportive of some housing outside settlement boundaries where there is unmet need, and that strong local opposition or a site being outside a boundary is not on its own a reason to refuse. Leader Cllr Simon Morgan said any refusal must rest on sound planning evidence, and warned that unreasonable decisions can lead to costs being awarded against the council on appeal. In a second statement, the council explained that a National Scheme of Delegation in force since 31 October means many routine applications must now be decided by officers, and councillors can no longer call schemes in to committee.

The council says it has written to Housing Secretary Angela Rayner about the impact on rural districts. It agreed on 22 October to raise residents' speaking time at planning committee to five minutes, and says each application will still be judged on its merits, with highways, school and health advice from Essex County Council and the NHS.

stories.summary: The independent bookshop in Brentwood says sharp increases in its business rates and electricity bills have left it unable to carry on.

stories.headline: Harwich lifeboat volunteers treat unconscious crew member on commercial ship before helicopter airlift
stories.summary: An injured sailor with head injuries was winched from a commercial vessel at Bawdsey anchorage and flown to Ipswich Hospital after Harwich RNLI was called out.
body: Harwich RNLI's all-weather lifeboat was sent to help a crew member who had been knocked unconscious on board a commercial vessel at Bawdsey anchorage, off the Suffolk coast just north of Harwich, on Monday afternoon.

The lifeboat, Albert Brown, launched at about 1.28pm, Hits Radio reports. Two of its volunteer crew went aboard the ship to give first aid and prepare the injured sailor, who had head injuries, to be taken off. The casualty was then winched up into a helicopter.
The helicopter flew the sailor to Ipswich Hospital, the BBC reports. No update on the sailor's condition has been given, and the lifeboat returned to its Harwich station once the job was done.
points: Harwich all-weather lifeboat Albert Brown launched at about 1.28pm on Monday
Two RNLI volunteers boarded the commercial vessel to treat the casualty
Injured crew member winched into a helicopter and flown to Ipswich Hospital

stories.headline: c2c trains to call at Purfleet, Rainham and Dagenham Dock again from Wednesday after Barking derailment repairs
stories.summary: Passenger services through the stretch shut since a freight train came off the tracks near Barking on 23 October are due back on Wednesday 11 November, ending almost three weeks of rail replacement buses for Purfleet commuters.
body: c2c says passenger trains will resume calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham and Purfleet from Wednesday 11 November, after the line near Barking was closed by the derailment of a GB Railfreight train on 23 October. The closure has left Purfleet and Rainham passengers relying on replacement buses to Grays and Upminster for nearly three weeks.

RailAdvent reports that engineers have repaired more than 1.2km of track, including rebuilding a damaged set of specially made points. Network Rail has confirmed the reopening, which also brings back London Overground trains between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside. Rob Mullen of GBR Anglia said he was pleased passenger services would return on Wednesday.

Until then, trains do not stop at the three stations and passengers are advised not to travel from them. Rail replacement buses run between Upminster and Grays via Rainham and Purfleet, and tickets are accepted on Greater Anglia and on TfL buses. Separately, London-bound trains are still not stopping at Limehouse while work continues there.
points: Line near Barking shut since a freight derailment on 23 October
More than 1.2km of track and a set of points repaired
Replacement buses Upminster to Grays run until services resume
London-bound trains still not calling at Limehouse

stories.headline: Saffron Walden recycling centre on Thaxted Road reopens today after ten-day closure
stories.summary: Essex County Council confirmed on Tuesday evening that the tip would open as usual from Wednesday 11 November, after a worker was hurt on site.
body: Saffron Walden Recycling Centre on Thaxted Road reopens to the public today, Wednesday 11 November, Essex County Council has confirmed. The site had been shut since a male employee was injured there on Saturday 31 October. An air ambulance landed at the centre, but he was taken to Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge by road, the Bishop's Stortford Independent reports. The council thanked residents for their patience.
points: Air ambulance landed at the site, but he went to Addenbrooke's by road
Council has not said what caused the injury

stories.headline: Walk-in X-rays and new scans coming to St Margaret's diagnostic centre in Epping from mid-December
stories.summary: Blood tests move into the new community diagnostic centre at St Margaret's Hospital on 16 November, with X-ray, ultrasound and liver scans following on 14 December.
body: Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust is expanding the community diagnostic centre at St Margaret's Hospital in Epping. Blood testing moves there from outpatients on 16 November, with room for about 230 patients a day, and two walk-in X-ray rooms open on 14 December for GP-referred patients.
A fourth ultrasound room and FibroScan liver checks also start on 14 December, adding about 350 patients a day. Chief executive Thom Lafferty called it an important step forward for diagnostic care.

Walk-in X-ray from 14 December, 8am to 7.30pm on weekdays

stories.headline: People sleeping rough in Essex offered free flu jabs for the first time, with clinics in Southend and Grays
stories.summary: NHS Essex is running dedicated clinics after national eligibility was widened to people aged 16 and over who are homeless.
body: People aged 16 and over who are sleeping rough or staying in hostels and night shelters can now get a free NHS flu vaccination, the first year the group has been eligible. NHS Essex is holding dedicated clinics in Southend on 12 November and Grays on 24 November.
No GP registration or fixed address is needed, and the jab is also available at taking-part pharmacies, GP practices and outreach services.

No GP registration or address needed

stories.summary: The figure from the 2025 residents survey appears in Thurrock Council's draft health and wellbeing strategy for 2027 to 2030, which councillors consider this week.
body: Fewer than half of people who answered Thurrock's 2025 residents survey said they feel safe after dark, the council's proposed health and wellbeing strategy shows. Community safety is one of its four priorities, alongside childhood, healthy lifestyles and ageing.
The council said detailed actions will follow in a delivery plan drawn up with partners, including Essex Police and the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner.

stories.headline: Microsoft picks Colchester City Council as the only UK council in its latest AI case study
stories.summary: The council says it measures how its staff use digital tools and targets training where confidence is low, rather than relying on technology alone.
body: Colchester City Council has been featured by Microsoft in a customer story about adopting AI and digital tools, and says it is the only UK council in the latest case study. The council says the work is aimed at helping staff work more efficiently and freeing up time for services to residents.

The council uses the WeChange.AI Navigator platform to see how employees engage with digital tools, alongside wider use of Microsoft 365 and AI-powered tools. It says the insights shape targeted support programmes, build digital confidence and strengthen a network of digital champions across its teams. Darren Kidson, the council's service director for digital, data and technology, said lasting change depends on staff having the confidence and support to work in new ways.

Cllr Alison Jay, portfolio holder for economic growth, transformation and digital, said successful AI adoption depends on people as much as technology, and that the recognition shows the role local government can play. The council did not publish figures for time or money saved, and says it will keep sharing what it has learned with other councils and public bodies.
points: Only UK council in Microsoft's latest AI and digital adoption case study
Uses the WeChange.AI Navigator platform to track staff use of digital tools

stories.headline: Basildon Council now expects a £3.8m overspend this year, with temporary housing for homeless families the biggest strain
stories.summary: A half-year report warns reserves of £41.1m could be largely used up by 2029/30 if gaps keep being covered from savings, though it calls that a scenario rather than a forecast.
body: Basildon Council's general fund is forecast to finish 2026/27 £3.8m over budget, up £0.4m since June, according to a half-year report reported by Basildon Today. Housing accounts for £2.4m of the gap, £1.5m of it temporary accommodation, while the council housing account is £3.2m over.
Councillors on the finance scrutiny committee discuss the report on Monday 16 November before it goes to cabinet on 26 November.

Council housing account £3.2m over, improved from £4.5m in June

stories.summary: A motion from the Mayor of Basildon goes to full council on 17 November, asking officers to look at sites, designs and funding for a memorial for Basildon and Laindon.
body: Basildon Council will vote on Tuesday 17 November on whether to back a permanent war memorial for Basildon and Laindon, a cause championed by D-Day veteran Don Sheppard, who died in 2024 aged 104, Basildon Today reports.
If passed, officers would assess sites, designs, costs and funding and consult veterans' groups, the Royal British Legion and Mr Sheppard's family, with a report to cabinet within 30 days.

stories.summary: The East of England Ambulance Service says the jump reflects staff feeling more confident to report concerns, while a campaign group warns the true scale is likely higher.
body: The East of England Ambulance Service, which covers Essex, dismissed 25 staff over sexual safety cases in 2025/26, compared with four the year before, Local Democracy Reporting Service figures from the trust's annual report show. Reports more than doubled over the same period.

The trust told Essex County Council's health scrutiny committee it has brought in an independent body to review its complaints procedures; campaign group Surviving in Scrubs says the true scale is likely higher.

body: Saul Humphrey, Professor of Sustainable Construction Management at Anglia Ruskin University, is speaking at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, which runs until 20 November. As president of the Chartered Institute of Building he will chair a session on ideas such as digital twins and material passports, and join a panel on the skills builders need for a changing climate. ARU teaches construction management at its Chelmsford campus.

stories.headline: North Essex councils' joint Link scheme has backed 149 firms so far this year, 22 of them in Colchester
stories.summary: Most businesses helped had not used council-funded support in the previous year, Colchester City Council says, and a drop-in session for firms is planned in the city next month.
body: The North Essex Economic Board, a partnership of six councils, has supported 149 businesses so far this year through its Link programme, Colchester City Council said on Tuesday. It also ran 78 one-to-one advice sessions and drew 592 people to business masterclasses.

In Colchester, 22 businesses have been helped this year, including six one-to-one adviser sessions and four specialist time vouchers. Nearly eight in ten firms taking part had not used council-funded business support in the past 12 months. Councillor Alison Jay, Colchester's portfolio holder for economic growth, said the scheme showed the value of councils working together to support local firms.

Since it began in 2021 the programme has supported more than 2,428 businesses, held 237 events and invested over £2.35 million in economic growth, the council says. A business pop-in event is planned in Colchester on 2 December.
points: Six north Essex districts take part in the programme
592 people have attended its masterclasses this year
Business pop-in event in Colchester on 2 December

stories.headline: Family of St John's Hospital cleaner who died of mesothelioma ask former staff for asbestos information

body: Lillian Lamb, from Chelmsford, died in February at the age of 89, months after being diagnosed with mesothelioma late last year, according to law firm Leigh Day, which represents her family.

The firm says it is investigating whether asbestos was present at the former St John's Hospital in Wood Street, demolished in 2012, and is asking anyone who worked there to share what they remember about the building and working conditions.

councilwatch.headline: Government direction pushes Southend's draft local plan towards a six-week public consultation
councilwatch.summary: The new plan would set the rules for where homes go and how the council handles applications for shared houses, affordable housing and hot food takeaways.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet held an extraordinary meeting on 5 November 2026 to consider the final draft of the city's new Local Plan. A report from the Executive Director (Environment and Place) sought agreement to comply with a government direction by publishing the Regulation 19 Proposed Submission version of the plan for a consultation lasting at least six weeks. At this stage residents and others can comment on whether the plan is sound and legally compliant.

The minutes say national policy requires every council to keep an up-to-date local plan, which allocates sites for development and sets the policies used to decide planning applications. Councillors were told the existing Development Plan is out of date and no longer reflects major social, environmental and economic changes. The reasons recorded for the decision warn that without a plan development would not stop, but would be more likely to come forward in an uncoordinated and speculative way, with less supporting infrastructure and fewer protections for existing residents.

The papers say new criteria-based policies would give the council a more robust, evidenced approach to applications including Houses in Multiple Occupation, affordable housing and hot food takeaways. The meeting papers include the draft plan, a policies map, a report on the earlier Regulation 18 consultation, a sustainability appraisal and an updated Local Development Scheme setting out the timetable. Three questions from councillors were answered at the meeting and published with the minutes.
points: Extraordinary cabinet meeting held on 5 November 2026
Report sought agreement to publish the Regulation 19 draft plan under a government direction
Consultation to run for a minimum of six weeks, on soundness and legal compliance

councilwatch.headline: Auditors flag £1.7m pension difference in Southend's accounts but expect to finish on time
councilwatch.summary: KPMG told councillors its audit of the 2025/26 accounts is on track, with work still under way on the value of council homes.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's external auditor, KPMG, reported on its audit of the council's accounts for the year ended 31 March 2026 at the Audit and Governance Committee on 19 October 2026. KPMG said the work was progressing well and remained on track to be completed ahead of the statutory deadline. The committee noted the report.

Councillors were told of a £1.7 million unadjusted audit difference relating to pension liabilities, along with several control findings on property valuations and declarations of related party interests. Some risks identified at the planning stage had been removed after testing, but work was continuing on the valuation of council dwellings and on journal testing. Members asked about a fall in the value of council homes, proposed changes to the audit fee and how related party declarations are handled.

KPMG confirmed that officers had continued to support the audit and said there were no concerns about meeting the January 2027 deadline. At the same meeting the committee heard that a national financial resilience index placed Southend 30th of 62 comparable unitary councils, which officers described as a broadly average position.
points: Unadjusted audit difference of £1.7 million relating to pension liabilities

councilwatch.headline: Tendring households can now recycle glass at the kerbside after 70,000 extra boxes go out
councilwatch.summary: The council's environment lead told cabinet the expanded collections began on 5 October, and arts grants to the district have risen six-fold.
body: Tendring District Council's Portfolio Holder for Environment and ICT told the cabinet on 23 October 2026 that around 70,000 additional green recycling boxes had been delivered across the district. The expanded kerbside recycling service started on 5 October. Residents can now put out glass bottles and jars, along with a wider range of other materials, for collection from their homes.

The portfolio holder described the move from delivering the boxes to collecting the extra recycling from households as an important milestone, and said the change made recycling easier and more convenient for residents. The statement was made as one of the cabinet members' announcements, which the cabinet noted.

At the same meeting the Portfolio Holder for Arts, Culture and Heritage said Arts Council England had highlighted that National Lottery Project Grants investment in Tendring had grown from £85,000 in 2020/21 to more than £505,000 in 2025/26. The portfolio holder said the council's Connect Tendring cultural newsletter, launched this year, already has around 450 subscribers.

councilwatch.headline: Southend aims to bring council home repairs up to industry norms by Christmas after regulator judgement
councilwatch.summary: Electrical safety checks on council homes are now close to complete, but councillors heard that repairs remain the weak spot in Southend's response to the social housing regulator.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's Audit and Governance Committee received an update on 19 October 2026 on the council's progress in responding to a judgement by the Regulator of Social Housing. The report, from the Executive Director for Environment and Place, also covered the council's dealings with the Housing Ombudsman and the Building Safety Regulator.

The Head of Housing told the committee that monthly meetings with the regulator were continuing and that significant progress had been made on the council's Provider Improvement Plan. The council has reached 100% coverage of electrical safety checks in communal areas and 99% in homes, and the minutes say the regulator now regards electrical safety as business as usual. Repairs remain an area of focus, and a targeted improvement plan has been agreed with the council's repairs contractor to cut work in progress and bring performance up to industry norms by Christmas 2026.

Councillors were told the Housing Ombudsman's investigation has concluded, with the council due to submit a learning statement as the final stage. Officers said this was the first inspection under the new consumer regulation framework and that the council knew of areas needing improvement before the inspections took place. The committee asked for a further update on repairs performance.
points: Communal electrical safety check coverage: 100%; homes: 99%
Repairs contractor has a targeted improvement plan with a Christmas 2026 deadline

councilwatch.headline: Three in four Thurrock children entering care now get their first health check on time, up from 36%
councilwatch.summary: Councillors scrutinising children's services heard that initial health assessments within the 20-day legal deadline have more than doubled.
body: Thurrock Council's Children's Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee was told on 22 October 2026 that 75% of initial health assessments for children entering care are now completed within the statutory 20-day timescale. The figure compares with 36% previously, according to the minutes of the meeting.

Officers put the improvement down to closer joint working with Children's Services, more paediatric capacity and better oversight. They said late assessments were mainly caused by changes of placement, hospital admissions, missed appointments and occasional staff absence, and that only one delayed assessment in the reporting period was down to a lack of capacity.

The service is moving to a model led by specialist nurses working with paediatricians, and officers said a formal review in December 2026 will look at the views of children and families, the quality of assessments and timeliness. Councillors questioned whether enough paediatric capacity would remain, and officers said the aim was to use existing paediatric resources more effectively. The committee noted the update.

councilwatch.headline: Epping Forest councillors asked to back raising the top fly-tipping fine from £1,000 to £5,000
councilwatch.summary: A motion to full council called for the district's maximum fixed penalty for fly-tipping to rise fivefold now that the law allows it.
body: A motion put to Epping Forest District Council's full council meeting on 22 October 2026 asked councillors to support, in principle, raising the council's maximum fixed penalty notice for fly-tipping from £1,000 to £5,000. It was proposed by Councillor K Rizvi and seconded by Councillor C McCann. The published papers do not yet record the outcome.

The motion says the council can currently issue fines of up to £1,000 for fly-tipping, but recent changes to the law now allow councils to set a maximum of £5,000. It argues that people who deliberately dump waste should face a penalty reflecting the damage to the environment and the costs borne by residents.

If backed, the motion asks the Cabinet Member for Environment and Regulatory Services to work with the council's environmental enforcement team to bring in the higher fine as soon as practicable, subject to legal and constitutional requirements. It also calls for clear public communication and continued enforcement, and encourages residents to keep reporting fly-tipping with photographs, CCTV or dashcam footage where they have it.
points: Current maximum fly-tipping fixed penalty: £1,000

councilwatch.headline: Tendring set to adopt new protection plans for St Osyth and Manningtree and Mistley conservation areas
councilwatch.summary: Cabinet will decide on 13 November whether to adopt the final two of 20 conservation area appraisals, including revised boundaries.
body: Tendring District Council's cabinet will be asked on 13 November 2026 to adopt updated Conservation Area Character Appraisals and Management Plans for St Osyth and for Manningtree and Mistley. The report from the Portfolio Holder for Housing and Planning recommends adoption, including revised conservation area boundaries where applicable.

The report says both documents were shaped by public consultations held between 2022 and 2026, and that responses led to changes, including to some boundaries. Once adopted, the appraisals would become material planning considerations, meaning they would carry weight when planning applications in those areas are decided. They are the last two in a programme to review all 20 of the district's conservation areas, a priority of the Tendring Heritage Strategy, which includes five areas on Historic England's Heritage at Risk Register.

The report says that without adoption the council could not give weight to the updated appraisals in planning decisions, and its ability to conserve the district's historic environment would be reduced. The documents are also intended to inform the council's emerging Local Plan.

councilwatch.headline: Tendring adopts new skills and conduct standards for council housing staff after tenant feedback
councilwatch.summary: Cabinet adopted a policy setting out the skills, qualifications and conduct expected of housing staff, to meet a new regulator standard.
body: Tendring District Council's cabinet adopted a Housing Competence and Conduct Policy on 23 October 2026. The policy sets out the knowledge, skills, experience and behaviour expected of council housing staff and contractors, and includes a Housing Code of Conduct for staff.

The report says the policy is needed to comply with the Regulator of Social Housing's Competence and Conduct Standard, which requires landlords to have a written policy, and that failing to meet it could expose the council to regulatory scrutiny and enforcement. It covers recruitment, training, professional qualifications, appraisal and performance management. Tenants told the council their priorities were being treated with respect, being listened to, getting an empathetic response and being kept informed.

Tenant consultation on the code of conduct closed on 28 October 2026, and the cabinet authorised the Corporate Director (Operations and Delivery) to make changes in response, in consultation with the housing portfolio holder. The policy will be reviewed annually and no later than October 2027.
points: Adopted by cabinet on 23 October 2026

councilwatch.headline: Tendring budgets for life beyond 2028 as the government pauses the council shake-up
councilwatch.summary: With Whitehall reviewing its plan to replace Essex's councils, Tendring's cabinet has agreed to plan four years ahead, and backed money for toilets, playgrounds and housing staff.
body: Tendring District Council's cabinet has agreed to refresh the council's financial forecast over four years, to allow for the possibility that the council still exists after April 2028. That date had been the proposed start for a new unitary council under the government's original timetable for Greater Essex, but on 7 September 2026 the government announced it would pause and review its local government reorganisation programme.

The report to cabinet on 23 October said the pause had brought a significant level of uncertainty for the councils affected, though Tendring's two-year financial plan still left it in a positive position. If reorganisation goes ahead, even later than planned, the forecast can be switched back to the council's earlier approach of preparing for a handover to the new authority.

Cabinet also approved changes to this year's budget, including £540,000 for housing capacity and restructuring, £100,000 to invest in public toilets and £400,000 for project delivery capacity, and accepted £270,000 from the government's Playground Fund. The report said the general fund was £3.669m underspent against its profiled budget at the end of July, largely because of the timing of spending.
points: Forecast to be refreshed over four years in case the council continues beyond April 2028
Government paused its reorganisation programme on 7 September 2026
£270,000 Playground Fund grant accepted and £100,000 set aside for public toilets
General fund £3.669m underspent at the end of July, mostly down to timing

councilwatch.headline: Thurrock's special needs funding gap keeps growing as Treetops School plans 110 more places
councilwatch.summary: Children's services are on course to underspend by about £0.5m, but the grant that pays for special educational needs is heading deeper into deficit, councillors heard.
body: Thurrock Council's children's services are forecast to underspend by about £0.5 million this year, councillors on the Children's Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee heard on 22 October. Officers said the underspend came largely from making the most of grants and from staff vacancies, which offset rising demand, and that all planned savings had been achieved.

The committee was also told about pressure on the high needs block of the Dedicated Schools Grant, which pays for special educational needs provision. Officers said forecasts showed a growing deficit despite investment in local specialist places, and that national funding arrangements and reform proposals would be critical to its long-term sustainability, with government support expected to cover a substantial part of the deficit.

Officers confirmed that 110 additional places were planned at Treetops School through a phased expansion, which would add local specialist capacity and reduce reliance on placements outside the borough. They said feedback from the Department for Education on the council's submission had been positive, focusing on extra detail and measurable outcomes rather than finances. The committee noted the forecast.
points: Children's services forecast to underspend by about £0.5m
High needs deficit growing despite investment in local places
110 more places planned at Treetops School in a phased expansion
Government support expected to cover a substantial part of the deficit

councilwatch.headline: Thurrock picked as one of seven national pilots helping children stay with their wider family
councilwatch.summary: The Kinship Zones pilot will give practical, emotional and financial support to relatives raising children, as Thurrock reshapes its children's social care.
body: Thurrock has been selected as one of seven national Kinship Zones pilot authorities, councillors heard at the Children's Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee on 22 October. The pilot aims to help children stay safely within their wider family networks, with practical, emotional and financial support for kinship carers and fewer care proceedings.

It is part of the council's Families First Partnership programme, which aims to step in earlier and support whole families. Officers said ten Family Help Teams had been set up and a single assessment and planning framework introduced, and that work was under way on a Multi-Agency Child Protection Team bringing together professionals from partner organisations.

The committee also heard that 75% of initial health assessments for children entering care were now completed within the statutory 20 days, up from 36% previously. Officers credited closer joint working, more paediatric capacity and better oversight, and said a formal review of the new nurse-led and paediatrician model would take place in December 2026.
points: One of seven national Kinship Zones pilot authorities
Ten Family Help Teams now in place
75% of health checks for children entering care now on time, up from 36%
Review of the new health assessment model due in December

councilwatch.headline: Southend's fraud investigators have brought in more than £800,000 for the council this year
councilwatch.summary: School admissions fraud and Blue Badge misuse were among the areas councillors raised as the council's counter fraud team reported on its work.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's Counter Fraud and Investigation Team has generated benefits of more than £800,000 for the council so far this financial year, the Audit and Governance Committee heard on 19 October.

Councillors discussed recent work on school admissions fraud. Officers said referrals came from school admissions officers, members of the public and the team's own proactive investigations, and that growing public awareness had led to more referrals. Members also asked about Blue Badge enforcement and future investigation exercises.

The committee heard that a new fraud investigator had been recruited and that a number of investigations involving council employees were continuing. Officers said details could not be disclosed for confidentiality reasons, but that criminal prosecutions continued to be pursued where appropriate. The committee noted the report.
points: Benefits of more than £800,000 so far this financial year
More school admissions fraud referrals as awareness grows
Blue Badge enforcement raised by councillors
New fraud investigator recruited
